name: Broad bean
grown_as: A hardy annual vegetable, sown in autumn or early spring, grown for its green beans. Most varieties have white flowers with black blotches; a few (such as 'Crimson Flowered') are red. Drawn as the usual white-flowered kind. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: Upright, stiff, unbranched or with a few stems from the base, 60 cm to 1.2 m. The stem is square, hollow and hairless. No tendrils, so it does not climb; tall plants are held up with string. Leaves all along the stem, flowers clustered in the upper leaf joints.

leaf.type: Compound, pinnate: 2 to 6 leaflets (usually 2 or 3 pairs) on a short central stalk, which ends in a tiny soft point, not a tendril
leaf.leaflets: Leaflets with no stalks of their own, arranged in near-opposite pairs, the end pair larger. Each symmetrical.
leaf.outline: Each leaflet oval to elliptic, 4 to 8 cm long, broadest about the middle
leaf.tip: Rounded or blunt, sometimes with a tiny point
leaf.veins: Midrib with faint side veins looping near the edge; leaf looks smooth and fleshy
leaf.surface: Hairless, somewhat fleshy, with a grey-green waxy bloom
leaf.stalk: Short; at its base a pair of small, half arrow-shaped toothed stipules, each with a dark purple-black nectar spot

flower.form: A pea flower: an upright back petal (the standard), two side petals (the wings) and two lower petals joined into a boat-shaped keel between the wings
flower.petals: Five: a broad standard folded back, two wings and a keel hidden between them
flower.colour: White. Each wing petal has a large velvety black blotch; the standard has fine brown-purple lines toward its base.
flower.behind: A green bell-shaped calyx tube with five short teeth
flower.carried: In short clusters of 2 to 6 on very short stalks in the upper leaf joints, all facing out to one side, close against the stem
flower.season: April to June (autumn sowings earlier); strongly scented

fruit: Pods held upright at first, then leaning and hanging under their weight: thick, fleshy, 10 to 25 cm, green, slightly downy, lumpy over the beans, lined inside with white wool. Each holds 3 to 8 large flat beans. Ripe dry pods turn black and leathery. Seed: a large, flat, oblong bean 2 to 3 cm, buff or pale green, with a black or pale scar (hilum) along one end.
seedling: The seed leaves stay inside the bean underground. A thick square shoot comes up with a couple of small scale-like leaves, then the first leaves of one or two pairs of grey-green oval leaflets.
winter: Autumn-sown plants stand through winter as short young plants 10 to 20 cm with a few grey-green leaves; otherwise nothing.

leaf: 2 to 3 pairs of oval leaflets on a short stalk
no teeth and no tendril; the stalk ends in a tiny point
bloom: a pea flower with a white standard and wings
a large black blotch on each wing
fine dark lines on the standard
seed: a large flat oblong bean, buff or pale green
a long dark scar (hilum) across one end
seedling: a thick shoot with grey-green oval leaflets
young: an upright square stem with grey-green pinnate leaves
flower: white and black flowers in short clusters in the upper leaf joints
crop: thick green pods held upright or hanging from the leaf joints
seedhead: pods turned black and leathery, hanging or leaning
the plant browning and dying back

look_alikes: Field bean is the same species with smaller beans. Peas have huge leafy stipules and tendrils. Runner and French beans have three-leaflet leaves and twining stems.
